newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open barely changed.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open barely changed.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open little changed Thursday, based on market orders at 1019 EDT, dealers said.
USDA put new sales at 35,100 480-lb bales in the new 1997/98 crop, and at 93,100 bales in the old crop, for the week ended May 8.
Accumulated shipments reached 5.135 million bales for the 1996/97 crop, out of the USDA's export target of 7.0 million bales. Total commitments to date stood at 7,005,800 bales.
Market analysts view the report as neutral but said talk of dercertificated stocks could provide fundamental underpinning to the market.
Technically, July's ability to hold above 72.00 cents is viewed as positive. Traders are also anticipating a speculative short-covering rally in the near term.
Wednesday, most-active July ended 0.03 cent weaker at 72.30 cents per lb after trading from 72.40 to 72.05 cents. New-crop December finished 0.13 cent firmer at 74.61 cents.
Trade was estimated at a light 4,000 lots.
